detail.longDescription: I’m trying to understand how Playwright locators behave when a page re-renders an element after an action. For example: const button = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }); await button.click(); // The application re-renders the button here. await button.click(); In this example, the application replaces the original button element in the DOM after the first click. I understand that Playwright locators are evaluated when an action is performed rather than storing a reference to a particular DOM element. Does the second click resolve the locator again and target the newly rendered button? If so, is there any situation where I should create a new locator after the re-render? I’m trying to understand the recommended Playwright behavior when an element matched by a locator is replaced during a test.
